parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans expression, legal gender recognition since 2013 without surgery, hate-crime law covering gender identity, open military service, multiple LGBT centres, mayors backing Prides, and a travel guide reporting wide acceptance of LGBTQIA+ visitors. Enforcement is the weak point: NGOs document uneven discrimination-case handling, inadequate hate-crime investigations, under-reporting, victims fearing report processes, plus escalating anti-gender political rhetoric and one disrupted Pride — tier-5/paper-protection friction rather than state threat. A 2026 legal article notes practical search difficulties for gender-nonconforming people; that is a conditional edge case, not a universal birth-sex mandate. Nothing documents border/document friction, facility exclusion, custody rules, police targeting or organised violence — these are open questions, not exposures. Prosecution of an accommodation refusal shows remedies sometimes operate. Net: acceptance plus imperfect enforcement, above mid-tier but below the consistently-remedied acceptance profiles.
